application_review: The harmonic mass in a fixed multiplicative bin has the exact tail-independent logarithmic main term and an absolute discretization error at most t/Q. For W <= Q this yields relative error at most 2*q*t/W, hence at most 2*C*q/R when W=tlo*R and t<=C*tlo.

When the relative error is at most one half, every allowed tail product has pivot mass between one half and three halves of the same positive main term. Any two such masses differ by a factor at most three. These are finite inequalities, without an asymptotic or nonempty-residue-class assumption.

The original finite conditional joint mass satisfies an exact Bayes event formula. A positive common lower likelihood bound proves a positive conditioning denominator; a corresponding upper bound proves domination for every event of the outside variable, even when the inner laws depend on that variable.

For the original raw harmonic pivot mass, a bin entirely within its cutoff and a prescribed unit residue modulo a multiple of the roughness modulus have event mass exactly equal to the residue harmonic sum divided by the original harmonic normalizer. Thus conditioning the actual joint law on the short bin and pivot residue multiplies every tail-event probability by at most three under the explicit scale inequalities.

Reviewed the relative-error derivation: the logarithmic main term is strictly positive and independent of the tail product; the inequality log((Q+W)/Q)>=W/(Q+W) together with W<=Q supplies the stated explicit constant.

Reviewed conditioning non-vacuity: the finite Bayes proof establishes a strictly positive denominator from a normalized nonnegative outside prior and the positive common likelihood lower bound. No small-denominator conditioning conclusion is assumed.

Reviewed actual pivot law: interval membership uses real endpoints with natural ceiling and exact half-open inequalities. Modulus divisibility and a unit residue prove the original roughness condition; full cutoff containment prevents omitted weights. The original harmonic normalizer is shared by all tail products.

Reviewed scope: only short-bin and residue conditioning is performed, not exact microcell conditioning. Factor-three domination is relative to the original outside prior; domination by a product of uniform dyadic residue laws and discarded-bin probabilities are not yet claimed.
